title: Peated Scotch
subtitle: Peat smoke in Scotch whisky
description: Why Scottish distillers dried their malt over peat, and how Glenmorangie, Bowmore, Caol Ila and Ardbeg came to use a great deal of it or none. Four pours.

pours.name: Glenmorangie The Original
pours.notes: Malt with next to no peat in it. Keep a little back to compare with the last pour.

pours.name: Bowmore 12
pours.notes: Usually described as medium peated. Taste it beside the Glenmorangie: same age and strength, different kiln.

pours.name: Caol Ila 12
pours.notes: Malt largely from Port Ellen, and a whisky made mostly for blending. Notice how dry the smoke is next to the Bowmore.

pours.name: Ardbeg Ten
pours.notes: The main bottling after the 1997 restart. Try it neat, then with a few drops of water, then go back to the Glenmorangie.
